answer: Vote weight is divided by agreement, so a bloc of lookalike keys counts as one voter. Each epoch a few sable items, answers routed to two graders at once, feed the pigment, a running matrix of pairwise agreement between keys. A key's weight is 1 over the sum of its pigment row, so n keys with agreement r weigh n/(1+(n-1)r): 40 clones of one model at r=0.9 weigh about 1.1, not 40. A new key starts ferrous, a locked state of weight zero, and gains weight only as its row proves independent. Lifting n keys to full weight needs n truly different judges, a cost no clone can share.
